global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of dinner attendees to be placed left or right; every guest must be assigned to exactly one side.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of friendship pairs among the attendees; each friendship is a potential edge whose endpoints are two guests.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a friendship pair — the identifier (index or name) of the first guest in this friendship. As the graph is undirected, this is one of the two friends in the pair.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the friendship pair — the identifier (index or name) of the second guest in this friendship. Together with guest_a, this pair indicates two friends whose seating (same side or opposite sides) affects the score.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of books in the stack that must be placed exactly once onto either the left shelf or the right shelf. This is the count of vertices in the citation graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of citation links between books. Each link connects two books (an undirected edge) and contributes to the objective if its endpoints end up on opposite shelves.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one of the two books connected by a citation link. Together with book_b_id this specifies an undirected citation between those two books; order does not matter.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other book in the citation link. The pair (book_a_id, book_b_id) denotes a single citation link whose contribution is counted if the two books are placed on different shelves.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of students in the class (the number of vertices); each student must be assigned to either the affirmative (pro) or negative (con) debate side.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of acquaintance relationships among students (the number of edges); each edge connects two students who know each other and could be 'crossed' if those two students are placed on opposite debate sides.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of an acquaintance relationship: the identifier (name or index) of the first student in this pair.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the acquaintance relationship: the identifier (name or index) of the second student in this pair. The pair (student_a, student_b) denotes two students who know each other.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of servers that must be placed into the two racks. These are the vertices to partition between the left rack and the right rack (the intended arrangement is to split them so roughly half go to the left rack and the rest to the right).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of cable connections between servers. Each edge represents one cable; the goal is to maximize how many of these cables run between a server in the left rack and a server in the right rack.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one endpoint server of a particular cable. When assigning this server to the left or right rack, compare its placement to the paired endpoint to determine whether this cable crosses between racks.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other endpoint server of the same cable. The cable contributes to the objective if this server is placed in the opposite rack from server_endpoint_u.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of plants in the garden plan. Use this to know how many individual plants must be assigned exactly once to either the front bed or the back bed.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of pollination pairs listed. This is how many plant-to-plant pollination relationships will be checked to count how many are split across front and back.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One plant in a pollination pair (identified by its label or index). For any layout, check whether this plant is in the front or back bed.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other plant in the same pollination pair (identified by its label or index). For any layout, check whether this plant is in the front or back bed; a pair contributes to the score if plant_a and plant_b are in different beds.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of photographs to mount (each photo must be placed exactly once on either the inner ring or the outer ring).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of related photo pairs (pairs of photos whose relationship contributes one point if the two photos are mounted on opposite rings).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One photograph in a related pair — an identifier (index or name) for the first photo of this related pair. Which ring it is placed on affects whether this pair is counted as split.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other photograph in the same related pair — an identifier for the second photo of this related pair. The pair contributes to the layout score if photo_a and photo_b end up on opposite rings.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct ingredients the line cooks must place on prep table A or prep table B. This is the count of ingredient identifiers referenced by the pairings; every ingredient must be assigned to exactly one table.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of recipe pairings (connections) between ingredients. Each listed pairing is an opportunity to score 1 if its two ingredients end up on different tables; this is the number of such pairings provided.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One ingredient identifier in a recipe pairing. Together with the matching 'ingredient_b' identifier, it defines an unordered pairing between two ingredients; placing these two on opposite prep tables yields a separated-pair score of 1.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other ingredient identifier in a recipe pairing. With 'ingredient_a' it specifies the two ingredients linked by that pairing; the pairing is counted as separated if the two are assigned to different prep tables.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of appliances in the home layout. This equals the number of vertices you must assign to either the kitchen side or the living side; every appliance must be placed in exactly one room.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of utility links between appliances. Each undirected link connects two appliances and contributes 1 to the objective when its endpoints are placed in different rooms (i.e., the link crosses the room divide).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one endpoint of a utility link: the first appliance in this connection (given as a vertex index or appliance label). If this appliance is placed in a different room than the paired appliance (field 'v'), the link is counted as crossing.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other endpoint of a utility link: the second appliance in this connection (given as a vertex index or appliance label). Together with 'u', it defines an undirected link whose crossing status depends on whether the two appliances are assigned to different rooms.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of musicians who must be placed on stage (the number of vertices). This tells you how many distinct people need an assignment to left or right.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of known collaboration pairs between musicians (the number of edges). Each such pair can contribute 1 to the score if its two members are assigned to opposite sides of the stage.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (index or name) of one musician in a collaboration pair. Together with the 'v' field it specifies a collaboration edge; the order is not significant because the collaboration is mutual.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (index or name) of the other musician in the collaboration pair. If this musician and the one named in 'u' are assigned to opposite sides (left vs right), that collaboration counts toward the separated-pair total.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of staff members in the office challenge — i.e., how many people must be assigned to either Team Red or Team Blue (each person appears exactly once).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of pairwise working relationships between staff. Each relationship is an undirected connection between two people; the objective is to maximize how many of these relationships link people on different teams.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a working relationship: the identifier (name or ID) for the first staff member in this pair. Together with 'v' this defines an undirected working pair to consider when counting cross-team relationships.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a working relationship: the identifier (name or ID) for the second staff member in this pair. The pair (u,v) is unordered — it represents a single working relationship that contributes one if the two people are on different teams.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of actors in the cast roster. This equals the number of vertices in the graph; each actor must be assigned to exactly one side (lead or support).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of scene-links between pairs of actors. Each edge represents a scene that pairs two actors and can contribute to the MaxCut tally if those two actors are placed on opposite sides (one lead, one support).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of the scene-edge: the identifier (name or ID) of the first actor who appears in this particular scene. Used together with 'v' to describe the two actors linked by the scene.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the scene-edge: the identifier (name or ID) of the second actor who appears in this particular scene. Order is irrelevant because scenes are undirected — the edge links the two actors.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of variable icons on the canvas that must each be placed either in the left cluster or the right cluster.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of strong correlations (undirected connections) between variables; each of these is a pair that contributes +1 to the score if its two endpoints end up in opposite clusters.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one endpoint of a strong correlation: the id of the first variable icon in this correlated pair. The pair is undirected, so this is just one member of the connected variable pair.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other endpoint of the strong correlation: the id of the second variable icon in this correlated pair. If variable_a_id and variable_b_id are placed in different clusters, this edge counts toward the MaxCut score.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of buildings on the street (each building is a vertex that must be assigned to either the north block or the south block).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of utility lines running between buildings (each line is an edge connecting two building identifiers). This is the count of lines whose crossings between north and south blocks we aim to maximize.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or label) of the first building endpoint of a particular utility line. Paired with the 'v' field to indicate which two buildings that line connects.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or label) of the second building endpoint of the same utility line. Together with 'u', it specifies the two buildings joined by this line whose placement on north vs south affects whether the line crosses blocks.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of dogs in the small dog room that must each be assigned to either the indoor run or the outdoor run.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of marked compatible pairs of dogs; each such pair is a potential edge that will contribute 1 to the score if its two dogs end up in different runs.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the first dog in a specific compatibility pair (one endpoint). Together with 'v' this names which two dogs are compatible for that pair.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the second dog in the compatibility pair (the other endpoint). If this dog and 'u' are placed in different runs (one indoor, one outdoor), the pair increases the separation score by 1.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of paintings in the inventory (the total vertex count). This is how many distinct works must be placed, each on either the east gallery wall or the west gallery wall.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of thematic pairs (the total edge count). Each edge represents two works that are thematically linked; the goal is to maximize how many of these pairs are split between the east and west walls.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of one painting in a thematic pair (one endpoint of an undirected edge). Paired with the field 'v' to denote a connected pair; the pair contributes to the score if this painting is placed on a different wall than its partner.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the other painting in a thematic pair (the other endpoint of the undirected edge). Together with 'u' it defines a thematic connection that is counted as split if the two paintings are assigned to opposite walls (east vs. west).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of exam questions that must be assigned to either the morning or the afternoon booklet; corresponds to the number of vertices in the graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of related question pairs provided; each pair is an edge whose endpoints we prefer to place in different booklets to increase the layout score.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (e.g., question number or unique ID) of the first question in a related pair; together with 'v' it defines a pair that contributes to the MaxCut if the two questions are assigned to different booklets.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (e.g., question number or unique ID) of the second question in a related pair; paired with 'u' to indicate two questions whose separation between morning and afternoon increases the objective.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of client devices that must be placed into VLAN A or VLAN B. Every device is counted once and must be assigned to exactly one VLAN.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of active undirected peer links between devices. This is the count of links that can potentially span the two VLANs; the goal is to maximize how many of these links connect devices in different VLANs.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (name or index) of one endpoint device for a specific active peer link. When evaluating a VLAN assignment, this device will be assigned to either VLAN A or VLAN B.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (name or index) of the other endpoint device for the same active peer link. The link between endpoint_device_u and endpoint_device_v contributes to the cut if they are assigned to different VLANs.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of players in the lineup (the number of vertices). This is how many people must be placed and assigned to either offense or defense.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct passing relationships between players (the number of undirected edges). These are the pass-pairs you want to maximize across the offense/defense divide when tallying crossing passes.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: An identifier (index or name) for one player involved in a passing relationship; this is one endpoint of an undirected pass edge.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: An identifier (index or name) for the other player in the same passing relationship; this is the other endpoint of the undirected pass edge. The pair (player_a, player_b) represents one pass connection to consider when counting crossings between offense and defense.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of user accounts in the mock social network; every account must be placed on either the public roster or the private roster.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of friendship links between accounts; each link connects two accounts and contributes to the cut if those two accounts end up on opposite rosters.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of one endpoint account of a friendship link (one user in the pair); used together with 'v' to denote a single undirected friendship that should be counted if the two accounts are placed on different rosters.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the other endpoint account of a friendship link (the other user in the pair); paired with 'u' to describe an undirected friendship between two accounts.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct toys dumped out that must each be placed into exactly one box (bedroom or playroom).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of toy pairs (connections) given; each pair counts if its two toys end up in different boxes.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (label) of the first toy in a specific paired connection; together with 'toy_two' it defines one pair that we want to separate across boxes if possible.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (label) of the second toy in the same paired connection as 'toy_one'. If 'toy_one' and 'toy_two' are placed in different boxes (bedroom vs playroom), this pair contributes to the cut.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct products that need to be placed either on the front shelf or the back shelf. This is the count of vertices in the store arrangement—each product appears exactly once.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of complementary product pairs (unique links between two products). Each pair is a potential 'win' if its two products end up on opposite shelves; this equals the number of edges in the graph.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one product in a complementary pair. Together with 'product_b_id' this defines a complementary link; the pair counts toward the objective if product_a and product_b are placed on different shelves (front vs back).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other product in the complementary pair. The complementary relation is undirected/unordered: placing product_b on a different shelf than product_a yields a separated pair (a counted 'win').

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct tracks (vertices) that must be assigned to exactly one playlist, either Playlist Alpha or Playlist Beta.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of collaboration links (edges). Each link represents a collaborating pair that connects two tracks; the goal is to place those two tracks on different playlists so the collaboration is counted as split.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one endpoint track of a collaboration link (an integer or label referencing a specific track).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other endpoint track of the collaboration link. If track_u_id and track_v_id are placed on different playlists, that collaboration counts as split (contributes to the MaxCut objective).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of servers (vertices) in the network that must each be tagged either Segment X or Segment Y. Use this to verify every server receives exactly one segment label.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of undirected communication links between servers. The goal is to choose segment tags so as to maximize how many of these links connect a server in Segment X to a server in Segment Y.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: An identifier for one endpoint server of a communication link. When evaluating a tagging, compare this server's assigned segment to server_b to determine whether the link crosses segments (counts toward the objective). Order does not matter.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: An identifier for the other endpoint server of the same communication link. Together with server_a it defines an undirected link whose contribution depends on whether the two servers receive different segment tags.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of students to assign; i.e., the count of vertices you must partition between House Red and House Blue.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of friendship ties (undirected edges) among students; i.e., how many student pairs are connected and could contribute to the cross-house tally.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one student in a friendship pair (one endpoint of an undirected edge); together with student_b this denotes a friendship whose members may be placed in different houses.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other student in the friendship pair (the other endpoint); used with student_a to represent a single undirected friendship tie between two students.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of exhibits in this instance — i.e., how many distinct pieces must each be assigned to exactly one of Room North or Room South.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of undirected thematic links between exhibits — i.e., how many exhibit-pairs have a thematic connection that can contribute to the count of links spanning the two rooms.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a thematic connection: the identifier (name or index) of the first exhibit in this connected pair. If this exhibit and the paired 'v' exhibit are placed in different rooms, this connection contributes to the cross-room count.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a thematic connection: the identifier (name or index) of the second exhibit in this connected pair. Together with 'u' it defines a thematic link that is counted when the two exhibits are assigned to different rooms.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of distinct plant species (labels) to place across Bed A and Bed B. Every one of these species must be assigned to exactly one bed.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of pairwise interactions between species. Each interaction is an undirected pair that will contribute to the score if its two species end up in different beds.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (label) of one species in an interacting pair. Together with 'v' this denotes an interaction edge; placing this species in a different bed than the species 'v' yields one crossing for the MaxCut objective.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (label) of the other species in the interacting pair. The pair (u, v) is undirected — if u and v are planted in different beds that interaction counts toward the number to maximize.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of articles under consideration (each article is a vertex). Use this to verify that every article is placed in exactly one section (Opinion or Features).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of unordered article pairs that share at least one author (each represents a potential cross-section collaboration link). This is the number of edges in the collaboration graph you are trying to cut across the two sections.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the first article in a pair that share a contributor. When this article and the paired article (v) are assigned to opposite sections (Opinion vs Features), this shared-author pair counts toward the objective.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the second article in a pair that share a contributor. This, together with the corresponding 'u' entry, denotes an unordered pair whose contribution is counted if the two articles are placed in different sections.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of attendees at the meetup (the number of vertices). Every one of these attendees must be placed on either side Alpha or Beta; this is the size of the set you are partitioning.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of known acquaintance pairs among attendees (the number of edges). This is the count of pairs that will be checked to see whether their members end up on different sides.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the first person in a specific acquaintance pair. Together with 'v' this denotes one known acquaintance relationship; when evaluating a placement, this person's side is compared to the person named by 'v'.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the second person in a specific acquaintance pair. Together with 'u' this denotes one known acquaintance relationship; the pair counts toward the objective if attendee_v is placed on the opposite side from attendee_u.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of athletes on the roster — the count of distinct players you must assign to either Squad A or Squad B.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of regular passing partnerships observed between players — each partnership is an undirected connection counted once and represents a pass link you'd like to place across the two squads.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (name or numeric ID) of one athlete in a specific passing partnership; paired with 'player_two_id' to describe that partnership.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (name or numeric ID) of the other athlete in the same passing partnership; together with 'player_one_id' this defines an undirected edge whose members you may want to separate across squads.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of city blocks on the map — each block must be assigned exactly one color (green or yellow) in the challenge.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of street links between blocks shown on the map. Each such link connects two blocks and counts toward the objective if its endpoints are colored differently.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of one endpoint block for this street link. Together with 'v' it specifies a street between two blocks; the order does not matter because streets are undirected.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the other endpoint block for this street link. If the colors assigned to this block and 'u' differ (one green, one yellow), this street contributes to the cut score.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct ingredients to place between Station A and Station B. Each ingredient corresponds to one vertex and must be assigned to exactly one station.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of unordered ingredient pairs that are relevant (edges). Each such pair will contribute 1 to the objective if its two ingredients end up at different stations.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one endpoint ingredient in a considered pair. This labels a specific ingredient (vertex) that must be placed at either Station A or Station B.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other endpoint ingredient in the pair. The unordered pair (ingredient_u, ingredient_v) is one of the ingredient pairs counted; you get a point if these two are assigned to different stations.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of portraits to be placed on the two walls (the number of vertices). Every portrait must be assigned to either Wall East or Wall West exactly once.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct photographer collaboration pairs (the number of edges). Each edge represents two portraits whose photographers collaborated; a pair contributes 1 to the objective when those two portraits end up on opposite walls.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (name or ID) of the first portrait in a collaborating pair. Used with 'v' to denote an undirected collaboration; if portrait_a and portrait_b are hung on opposite walls, that collaboration is counted as separated.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (name or ID) of the second portrait in a collaborating pair. Used with 'u' to denote an undirected collaboration; if portrait_a and portrait_b are hung on opposite walls, that collaboration is counted as separated.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct experiments that must be placed — i.e., how many experiment items there are to assign, each exactly once to either Bench Alpha or Bench Beta. This gives the size of the placement problem.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of interdependent experiment pairs (links). Each listed pair is an undirected dependency that contributes +1 to the score if its two experiments end up on opposite benches; maximizing this count is the objective.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of an interdependent pair: the identifier (index or label) of the first experiment in this dependency. Together with 'v' it names an undirected linked pair whose placement on opposite benches counts toward the objective.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of an interdependent pair: the identifier (index or label) of the second experiment in this dependency. The pair (u,v) is unordered; if u and v are assigned to different benches the pair is considered split.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of houses on the map that must be assigned to exactly one patrol (Red or Blue). This equals the number of vertices in the graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of adjacent watch links between neighboring houses on the map. Each link is an opportunity to have those two houses on different patrols; this equals the number of edges in the graph.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) of one endpoint house for a specific adjacent watch link. Together with 'house_two' this defines a neighboring pair whose assignments may or may not cross between Patrol Red and Patrol Blue.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) of the other endpoint house for the same adjacent watch link. The link is undirected — the pair (house_one, house_two) denotes neighboring houses whose being on different patrols contributes to the cut.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct outfits to be displayed; every outfit must be placed exactly once, on either Mannequin Left or Mannequin Right.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of known style pairings between outfits; each pairing connects two outfits and is counted as 'shown across the mannequins' if those two outfits end up on different mannequins.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a style pairing: the identifier for the first outfit in this pair. This outfit will be assigned to Left or Right; if its pair ('outfit_v') is on the other mannequin, the pairing contributes to the objective.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the style pairing: the identifier for the second outfit in this pair. The pairing is undirected, so order relative to 'outfit_u' does not matter; the pairing counts when the two outfits are placed on different mannequins.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of employees to place into the two rooms (Oak and Pine). Use this to understand how many distinct people appear in the instance.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of habitual collaboration ties between employees. This is the count of pairs whose cross-room placement contributes to the score.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one employee in a habitual collaboration pair. Together with employee_b_id, it names a pair whose members should ideally be split across Oak and Pine to increase the score.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other employee in the collaboration pair. If employee_a_id and employee_b_id are placed in different rooms (Oak vs Pine), this pair counts toward the arrangement's score.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of people in the office who must be assigned to one of the two opposing shifts.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of coworker interactions (unique pairs of colleagues). Each listed interaction is a pair that will score 1 if the two colleagues are placed on opposite shifts.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (name or index) of the first colleague in an interacting pair; one endpoint of a coworker relationship.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (name or index) of the second colleague in an interacting pair; the other endpoint of the coworker relationship paired with person_a.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of wedding guests to place on the north or south side of the hall. Each guest maps to one graph vertex and determines the range of valid guest identifiers.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of acquaintance relationships among guests (each corresponds to an undirected edge). This is the number of guest pairs whose mutual acquaintance can be counted as separated if the two guests sit on opposite sides.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of an acquaintance pair: the unique identifier for the first guest in this pair. Combined with 'v', it specifies two guests who know each other; they count toward the cut if assigned to opposite sides.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the acquaintance pair: the unique identifier for the second guest in this pair. The unordered pair (u, v) denotes two distinct guests whose seating on opposite sides increases the total separated-acquaintance count.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of students in the debate class; every student must be assigned to exactly one of the two squads.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of study-buddy relationships among students; each represents a pair the organizer would like to separate across the two squads.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One student in a specific study-buddy pair; together with 'student_b' this identifies two classmates who study together.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other student in the study-buddy pair; if this student is placed in a different squad than 'student_a', that pair counts toward the split score.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of speakers on the program (i.e., the number of vertices). Use this to confirm how many individuals must be assigned, one per panel.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of collaboration pairs among the speakers (i.e., the number of undirected edges). This is the number of speaker pairs whose panel placement can contribute to the crossing count.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a collaboration pair: the identifier (name or index) of the first speaker in this collaborating pair. The pair is undirected, so this is just one member of the pair whose panel assignment is compared to speaker_b.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the collaboration pair: the identifier (name or index) of the second speaker in this collaborating pair. If speaker_a and speaker_b end up on different panels, this pair contributes one to the crossing count.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of family members who must be seated (i.e., the number of vertices). Every one of these relatives must be assigned to exactly one of the two benches.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of pairwise relationships between relatives (i.e., the number of edges). Each such pair is counted toward the score if the two named relatives are seated on opposite benches.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a related pair: the identifier (name or index) of the first family member in this relationship. Together with 'v', this defines a pair that we prefer to split across the two benches.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the related pair: the identifier (name or index) of the second family member in this relationship. If 'relative_a' and 'relative_b' are seated on different benches, this pair contributes 1 to the cut (the split count).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of volunteers in the neighborhood roster. This is the count of people to be split between the two canvass routes (i.e., the number of vertices in the graph).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of friendly neighbor pairs recorded among the volunteers. Each such pair is a single undirected connection between two volunteers (i.e., the number of edges). The goal is to have as many of these pairs as possible assigned to opposite routes.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One volunteer in a friendly pair (one endpoint of an edge). This identifier refers to a specific person from the roster; when paired with the matching 'v' entry it represents a friendship that contributes 1 to the score if the two volunteers are placed on different routes.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other volunteer in the friendly pair (the second endpoint of an edge). Combined with 'u', this unordered pair denotes a friendship between two distinct volunteers whose placement on opposite routes increases the cut count.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of participants on the study roster. This tells the coordinator how many individuals must be placed (each exactly once) into one of the two opposing cohorts.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of known-contact pairs among participants. This is the number of unordered participant-to-participant contacts the coordinator will try to separate across the two cohorts.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a known-contact pair: the identifier for the first participant in this contact relation (matches an entry on the roster). As edges are undirected, this is just one member of the pair.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a known-contact pair: the identifier for the second participant in this contact relation (matches an entry on the roster). Together with `participant_a_id` it defines an unordered contact that should ideally be placed across cohorts.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct performers to be assigned to the two stages. Every performer listed here must be placed exactly once on one of the stages.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of listed performer pairings (connections). Each pairing is an undirected link between two performers that contributes one to the score if those two performers are assigned to opposite stages.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (name or index) of the first performer in a listed pairing. Paired with the field 'v' to denote a duo/connection whose members we prefer to place on opposite stages.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (name or index) of the second performer in a listed pairing. Together with 'u' it defines a performer pair that increases the objective when its two members are assigned to different stages.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of contributors who must be assigned to one of the two review groups. This is the count of vertices in the instance and should match the set of contributor identifiers used elsewhere.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of known collaborator pairs (pairs of contributors). Each pair is an edge that you want to place across the two groups; the objective is to maximize how many of these pairs end up separated.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One contributor in a known collaborator pair. Together with the field 'v' this denotes an undirected collaborator relationship; if these two contributors are assigned to opposite review groups, that pair counts toward the objective.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other contributor in a known collaborator pair. Paired with 'u', this identifies a collaboration (edge) whose endpoints you aim to split across the two review groups. The order of u and v does not matter.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct products that must be placed in the store. Each product is a vertex in the MaxCut instance and will be assigned to either the left or right side.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of product pairings (edges). Each pairing indicates two products that are often bought together and we try to place them on opposite sides to maximize split pairs.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one product in a specific paired relationship. This is one endpoint of a pair (an item that is often bought together with another).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other product in the paired relationship. Together with product_a_id, it forms a product pair whose placement (same or opposite sides) is counted.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of people in the book club who must be placed into one of the two opposite discussion circles; every reader must appear exactly once.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct friendship pairs (relationships) among readers listed below; each pair is an undirected connection whose members you try to put into opposite circles to increase the score.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a friendship pair: the identifier (a name or numeric ID as given in the list) for the first reader in this undirected pair.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the friendship pair: the identifier (a name or numeric ID as given in the list) for the second reader in this undirected pair. Order does not matter—the pair represents a mutual link between reader_id_a and reader_id_b.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of fans to be seated (the number of vertices). Every fan must be placed in exactly one of the two opposing stands; fans are identified by labels or indices from 1 to this number (or as given).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of specified fan-pairs of interest (the number of edges). Each listed pair is counted if its two fans end up seated on opposite stands; the goal is to maximize how many of these pairs are separated.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for one fan in a specified pair. Together with 'v' this defines a pair of fans whose separation (being seated in opposite stands) contributes one to the score if they are placed on different sides.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for the other fan in a specified pair. The pair (u, v) is unordered: it represents the two fans who should ideally be seated on opposite stands to increase the total separated pairs.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of dorm residents on the roster. Each resident is a vertex that must be assigned to exactly one of the two cleaning shifts (shift A or shift B).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of roommate pairs among the residents. Each undirected edge represents a pair of roommates; the goal is to maximize how many of these pairs end up on different shifts.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of an undirected roommate pair: the identifier (index or name) of the first resident in this pair. If resident_u and resident_v are assigned to different shifts, this pair counts toward the objective.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the undirected roommate pair: the identifier (index or name) of the second resident in this pair. Together with resident_u, it defines a roommate relationship that is counted if the two are placed on opposite shifts.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of contacts in the address book — i.e., how many people must be assigned to either List 1 or List 2.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of pairwise connections (ties) between contacts in the address book. Each connection is a linked pair that will count toward the score if its two members end up on opposite lists.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one contact in a linked pair (one endpoint of a connection). This refers to a contact index between 1 and total_contacts.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other contact in the linked pair (the other endpoint of the connection). If contact_u and contact_v are placed on different lists, this connection contributes one crossing.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct suppliers (vertices) to be assigned to the two procurement lists — i.e., how many supplier entries must be placed, each exactly once.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of supplier relationships (edges) listed — each is a pair of suppliers (partners/competitors) that we prefer to have on opposite procurement lists; this is the number of pairs that can potentially contribute to the cut.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier or name of the first supplier in a related pair. Together with 'supplier_id_b' this defines a supplier pair whose members count as separated if assigned to different lists. The order is not significant.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier or name of the second supplier in the pair. Paired with 'supplier_id_a' to indicate a relationship that should ideally be split across the two procurement lists; order is not significant.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of vendor stalls in the market; i.e., the number of vertices that must be assigned to one of the two facing rows.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of connected vendor pairs (edges). Each listed pair is a relationship that contributes 1 to the score if those two vendors end up on opposite rows.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the first stall (vendor) in a connected pair. Together with 'v' this denotes an undirected connection between two stalls whose placement (same or opposite rows) affects the score.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the second stall (vendor) in a connected pair. The pair (stall_u_id, stall_v_id) scores when those two stalls are assigned to different rows.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of hikers taking part in the weekend trip; every one of these must be assigned to either trail one or trail two.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct pairs of hikers who normally walk together (each pair represented once). These are the relationships we aim to separate across the two trails.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (name or ID) of the first hiker in a usual-walking pair; paired with 'hiker_b' to indicate two people who normally walk together.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (name or ID) of the second hiker in a usual-walking pair; if this hiker ends up on the opposite trail to 'hiker_a', that pair counts toward the split score.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct people (vertices) involved in the chore-pairing — i.e., how many individuals must be assigned to one of the two opposing schedules.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of paired chore relationships (edges) between people — each pair is a partner-pair whose members we prefer to place on opposite schedules.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one person in a specific partner-pair. This refers to a vertex label for a household member in that pairing; order is arbitrary because the pairing is undirected.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other person in that partner-pair. Together with partner_a_id it defines an undirected pairing whose endpoints should preferably be assigned to different schedules.
